# B research capital: uniform polynomial sampling after the qualifying noise time

**Release date: 8 November 2026.**

**Result:** a finite-bit, randomized, uniform-polynomial full-output sampler in the explicit qualifying-time regime below. This closes the previous repeated-recursion complexity gap. **The full all-time B goal remains open:** the unqualifying early/intermediate-time interval is not covered.

This is a theoretical construction, with two independent end-to-end mathematical reviews and reproducible checks of its algebraic components. It is not a formal machine-checked proof, a production sampler, a demonstrated practical speedup, or a historical priority claim. Human expert review is appropriate before an external theorem claim.

## The precise supported statement

Fix a rational constant rho_0 >= 0. The input consists of:

- n qubits on a finite subset of the square lattice;
- a **static**, rational Hermitian Hamiltonian with onsite and nearest-neighbor two-qubit terms;
- a rational bound h on each **grouped physical support**: sum all terms on the same site or edge before imposing this bound;
- an arbitrary rational product density matrix, pure or mixed;
- the same positive rational replacement rate gamma at every site, with h/gamma <= rho_0;
- rational time T >= 0 and requested total-variation error 0 < epsilon <= 1/2.

The evolution is

    L(rho) = -i[H,rho] + gamma sum_i (E_i(rho)-rho),
    E_i(rho) = (I_i/2) tensor Tr_i(rho).

Let tau = gamma T. A sufficient qualifying condition is

    r_8(tau) = 307584 + ceil(60 rho_0 tau),
    tau >= 76932 + 2 ceil(log_2 r_8(tau)).

For every fixed rho_0, all sufficiently large tau satisfy it. A separate late mixing shortcut also handles instances for which its certified error is small, even if the displayed condition is not needed. The h=0 case is the independent one-qubit noise law.

Within this scope, the construction samples the **entire joint computational-basis output distribution**, with unconditional TV error at most epsilon, using

    poly(B_input) (n/epsilon)^(C_rho_0)

bit operations and random bits. C_rho_0 is a finite computable constant, independent of n, epsilon and the supplied time. B_input includes all rational encodings and the site list. The polynomial degree is not claimed uniform if rho_0 grows with the input.

## Proposed uniform qualifying-time sampler theorem

Fix a rational upper bound rho_0 on the coupling-to-noise ratio and fix the two-body square-lattice locality convention. Let n qubits occupy a finite square-lattice region. Geometrically disconnected components are processed independently, with a divided TV error budget; no padding across arbitrarily large encoded coordinate gaps is allowed. Only connected activity/parent patches use the O(N^2) bounding-rectangle padding argument. The Hamiltonian is static, with one grouped rational Hermitian onsite term per site and one grouped rational Hermitian two-qubit term per nearest-neighbor edge, each of norm at most a supplied rational bound h. If the input supplies several contributions on the same physical support, they are first summed; h bounds that grouped sum, not each member of an arbitrarily long term list. A computable constant-dimensional entrywise bound can be used instead, changing only the fixed ratio constant. The input is an arbitrary rational product density, pure or mixed. Every qubit undergoes replacement noise at the same positive rational rate gamma:

    L(rho)=-i[H,rho]+gamma sum_i(E_i(rho)-rho),
    E_i(rho)=I_i/2 tensor Tr_i(rho),
    h/gamma<=rho_0.

If h=0, use the independent one-qubit replacement-noise law directly, with paid finite precision for exp(-tau), rather than dividing by a vanishing Hamiltonian scale in a regularity parameter. Equivalently a safe nonzero coefficient bound max(h,gamma) can be used in intermediate norm lemmas. Let T>=0 and 0<epsilon<=1/2 be rational, tau=gamma T, and let P be the full joint computational-basis output distribution after time T.

Use the original b=8 sufficient accumulated-noise contract, with Delta=5:

    r_8(tau)=307584+ceil(12 rho_0 Delta tau),
    tau>=76932+2ceil(log_2 r_8(tau)).

# Static noisy patch evaluation by exact rational coefficient MPOs

> Release-copy note: this historical proof/review snapshot has presentation-only edits recorded in SOURCE_PROVENANCE.json. Mathematical content is unchanged. Current status and superseded steps are identified in START_HERE.md and DEPENDENCY_MAP.md at the package root.

8 November 2026. Candidate proof, NOT independently cleared. The two central review targets are the growing-layer coefficient-rank import in Section 3 and the exact-rational gauge algorithm in Section 4. All proposed sampler consequences remain conditional on those targets. This is not an early-time full-output algorithm.

## 0. Target and input

A connected N-site subset of the square lattice has nearest-neighbor two-qubit Hamiltonian terms and onsite replacement noise. All entries, time t>=0 and desired scalar error eta in (0,1] are rational. The generator is written as a sum of complete local Lindblad generators; a Hamiltonian commutator on an edge counts as one such term. The sum of local diamond-norm bounds incident to a physical qubit is at most a fixed g. Numerical time and input bit lengths are explicitly charged. Product input rho and positive product effect A satisfy Tr rho=1 and Tr A=2^N. Therefore ||A||_infinity<=2^N.

We propose to evaluate G=Tr[A exp(tL)(rho)] to error eta. The intermediate MPO need not be CP or TP; it is a numerical approximation and is not passed off as a physical oracle. Set channel error epsilon=eta*2^(-N), and E=max(1,log(1/epsilon)).

For t<=polylog(N+2) and E=O(N polylog(N+2)), the proposed work is

    poly(input bits, t) * exp[O_g(N^(7/8) polylog(N+2))].

The explicit more informative exponent below is

    O(w b + (M/b) log(qM+w+2) + q log(M+1)
      + log(b+1) log(M+2)),

where w=O(N^(3/4)), b=Theta(N^(1/8)), q=O(N/b), and M=O(g t w b + E + log q). The constants in the exponent are independent of N, t, eta and the input denominator. This is subexponential in patch size, not polynomial in N.
